course_description:
Markets, market failures and externalities; economics of environmental pollution problems; economic measures for pollution control and environmental regulation. Environmental change, economic growth, natural resource depletion and population growth.

The purpose of this course is to introduce students to basic concepts and principles in environmental economics, and to demonstrate how these concepts can be used to provide insights into the design of policies which go some way towards addressing environmental problems at both local and global levels.

learning_outcomes.description: Apply economic theories and frameworks to critical environmental problems within the interdisciplinary industry.
Implement market and non-market tools and techniques to improve environmental quality and reduce environmental destruction.
Distinguish various environmental problems locally and globally to propose appropriate responses using the economic theories and frameworks.
Critically evaluate the environmental impact of decision-making using the economic approach and policy.
Communicate findings and solutions using diverse formats.

assessment_details.task_description: This assessment task requires students to work collaboratively in groups of four (4) to five (5) to design, produce, and present a podcast on a selected environmental issue. The topic must align with the key lecture themes covered in Weeks 10, 11, and 12 . This task is designed to develop students’ skills in communication, teamwork, critical thinking, and project management, while also providing an opportunity to create a professional-quality podcast as part of their academic portfolio. The assessment consists of three stages : Stage 1: Podcast Proposal (10%) Students will form groups and develop an initial proposal during their allocated tutorial in Week 4. Each student is required to submit an individual proposal using the prescribed template via Turnitin on Blackboard by the end of the sign-on tutorial. Three main themes will be provided for this assessment. Each theme will have a limited number of groups, and students must enrol in their preferred theme via Blackboard. Further details regarding theme allocation and the sign-up process will be provided in the first lecture . The proposal stage allows students to generate and explore ideas within their group, which will inform the development of the final group podcast. Stage 2: Podcast Recording Submission (15%) Groups are required to produce a 10-minute podcast recording based on their selected topic. The recording must be submitted by Friday of Week 10. This stage involves consolidating ideas developed during the proposal phase into a cohesive group output. Buddycheck will be used to support peer evaluation and will be due at the same time as the podcast submission. Stage 3 : Podcast Showcase and Reflection (5%) Podcast showcase sessions will be conducted during Weeks 11–13 , depending on topic allocation. Each group will present their podcast during their assigned session and participate in a Q&A discussion. Following the presentation, each student must submit an individual reflection via Turnitin on Blackboard during their allocated tutorial. Further details for each stage will be provided on Blackboard. Students should refer to the task sheet for comprehensive instructions and assessment criteria.
